# Print reality: the machine and the rules the machine imposes

## The machine

Flashforge Creator 5 Pro, 0.4 nozzle, corexy, four toolhead toolchanger
(`single_extruder_multi_material=0`). Its slicer, Flash Studio, is OrcaSlicer 2.3.2
under a `BambuStudio-01.10.01.50` header. Preset names: printer "Flashforge Creator 5
Pro 0.4 nozzle", process "0.24mm Standard @FF C5", filament pattern "Generic {TYPE} @FF
C5P". Bed defaults in the benches: 256 x 256 (COAMING's default; confirm before relying
on it for a full plate). Filament on hand: black, white and pink PETG; brand cream PETG
for the fourth slot.

Default layer 0.24 mm. Everything vertical quantises to it.

## Flush inlay only

No raised or embossed relief: the colour must be flush. Inlays are pockets in the body
filled by a separate part of the other colour, both printed in the same pass.

Depth rules (at 0.24 mm layers):

- dark over light hides in two layers (0.48 mm).
- light over dark needs about 1.2 mm (5 layers) or the dark shows through; pink over
  black the same: pink layers that are thinner at the top and bottom read as darkened
  pink, which is why the challenge coin went from 0.8 to 1.2 mm inlay and 3.2 to 3.6 mm
  thick.
- SPRUE's rule for two colour giveaways: white body, black inlay, 3 layers each face,
  because two layers of black hide white while white over black needs 1.2 mm.
- clamp the inlay so a solid core remains between the two faces.

Snap every depth, floor and ceiling to layer boundaries (`snapLayers`). Report layer
counts in the readout so the pause layer for an insert is obvious.

## Minimum feature and hygiene

0.4 nozzle: nothing thinner than about 0.6 mm prints reliably, gaps between colours
under about 0.35 mm smear. Defaults: min feature 0.6, stroke boost 0.15, despeckle at
0.35 x the min feature disc area, colour gap 0 (raise it when two bright colours share
a wall). See art-engine.md for the passes.

## Orientation and mirroring

The bed facing face is read from the other side once the part is flipped. Mirror its art
in X at slab time, keep the design as read in the state, and expect it to look backwards
in the slicer's bottom view. The challenge coin wordmark printed backwards before this
rule existed. Lid art on a folding case follows the laptop convention: upright to the
person across the table when the lid is open.

Print flat parts face down where the nicer face is the bed face; both halves of a case
open side up; lids inverted on their top face. No supports, no brims on anything with
socket mouths (a brim welds them shut). Everything prints as it is exported: the print
pose is the modelling pose, and volume parity between the two is the check.

## Rim and edge

A rim band runs the full thickness so the edge is one colour and frames both faces;
it follows the blank outline, not a circle. Edge treatments (reeds, knurl, rope) need
enough depth to survive the nozzle: 64 reeds at 0.5 mm deep printed practically round;
40 reeds at 1.0 mm deep with a 2.8 mm mouth on a 3.45 mm pitch read as knurls, with the
rim widened to 2.2 mm so the flute roots stay clear of the body colour.

## Insert pockets and pauses

NFC tag or magnet: a sealed internal pocket, tag diameter plus slack (26 mm for a 25 mm
sticker), 0.6 mm tall, floor and ceiling on layer boundaries, at least 0.6 mm floor and
0.8 mm roof. Compute and print the pause layer on the card: pause before the layer whose
z equals the ceiling. In the slicer: Preview tab, vertical layer slider, right click the
plus dot, Add pause (greyed out unless print order is by layer, not by object, and the
cursor is on the plus dot itself).

## Fits and clearances (MANDREL process loss table)

FDM: holes come out about 0.15 mm small, outer dims about 0.10 mm large. Bands: slide,
locate, press. Card slots: deck thickness plus 1 mm. Hinge axial clearance 0.6, pin
bore +0.6, print in place knuckle clearance 0.7 over the knuckle radius, 0.15 flats on a
rod so it does not roll. Quantise fits to layer and line multiples. Snap fingers
sized for a few newtons (SLATE went from 16 N to 6.8 N).

## Bridges and overhangs

Audit each part layer by layer in print orientation; classify unsupported regions as
bridge, ledge or overhang; the longest accepted bridge on PETG was 8.8 mm, ledges become
35 degree ramps, wide spans get a centre post. A back wall scallop left over from a
removed feature once became a full width 15 mm slot: the audit finds those, eyes do not.

## Time and material

Giveaways that print "a lot within an hour": 36 x 2.4 mm coins and 351 style picks
25.8 x 30.7 x 1.2 mm, mixed plates of 6 coins plus 20 picks, 12 coins, or 40 picks.
Masses on the print card use the real density from `materials.json` (PETG 1.27).

## The three materials that matter here

PETG for everything cosmetic (hack.build black / white / pink), TPU for flex and
grips, conductive PLA or TPU for FEELER sensors. Material choice per slot drives the
temperatures and speeds written into the 3MF; keep the table in `materials.json`
honest for the actual spools.
